scenes.headline: How a training run becomes checkable, step by step
scenes.sub: Gensyn's open-1b: a bit-exact hash after every optimizer step.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mesa! Open-1b is a small language model whose pretraining run can be replayed and checked, one step at a time. Here's how.

scenes.text: Make training bit-exact on any hardware, then hash the full training state after every step. A replay either reproduces the exact hash, or it doesn't.
scenes.say: The idea: make training bit-exact on any hardware, and hash the training state after every step. A replay either reproduces that exact hash, or it doesn't.

left.title: Proof-of-learning
items: Accepts a trajectory that lands close enough
left.say: Older proof-of-learning schemes accept a trajectory that lands close enough. Attackers learned to search inside that tolerance.

right.title: open-1b
right.say: Open-1b demands a bit-for-bit match across devices. There's no tolerance to hide in.

steps.say: Training ran on forty-eight H100s with RepOps kernels: one reduction order and one random number generator, the same on every backend.
After every step, the weights, optimizer moments, gradients and a batch digest are hashed, chained to the previous hash, and kept in one public log.
A checkpoint is published every hundred steps: eight hundred and ten of them.
An auditor loads one and replays the next steps on a single device, one virtual rank at a time. The new hash must equal the published one.

steps.note: one step: 25 minutes on an H100, 19 hours on an M4 Pro
steps.say: Checking a step still costs that step, redone on one device: twenty-five minutes on an H100, nineteen hours on an M4 Pro.
The hash chain covers pretraining, which ends at the base model.

steps.note: no public hash log for either stage
steps.say: Midtraining and SFT turn it into the chat model most people run. Neither stage is on the audit site.

scenes.text: Auditable here means not trusting a model is a concrete, byte-level exercise: replay a step, compare the hash.

recap: A hash after every step, in one public log
Replay any interval: the hash matches or not
scenes.say: To recap: bit-exact kernels, a hash for every step, and anyone can replay a step to check it.
